profile.campus: AWS / Talen Energy Susquehanna nuclear-adjacent campus, Berwick, Columbia County, PA
profile.address: Amazon AWS PHL, 1125, Electron Avenue, Berwick, Luzerne County, Pennsylvania, 18603
profile.reading:
This building sits on Electron Avenue at 1125, a mailing address of Berwick, Pennsylvania, though the parcel itself lies across the Susquehanna River on the grounds of the Susquehanna Steam Electric Station, a two unit nuclear plant in Salem Township, Luzerne County. The 300,000 square foot structure was built by Cumulus Data, a subsidiary Talen Energy created specifically to develop data center space on land it owned around the nuclear plant. Cumulus broke ground in December 2021 and announced the powered shell as complete in January 2023, describing it as the first of a planned campus of roughly six buildings meant to draw directly on the plant's low carbon output. Talen sold the entire 1,200 acre campus, including this first completed building, to Amazon Web Services in March 2024 for 650 million dollars, in what CoStar identified as the largest single commercial real estate sale in the United States that year.

What followed was a genuinely unusual regulatory fight, and it is worth recounting because it is the actual local and national record for this site. Talen and PJM Interconnection asked the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to approve an amended interconnection agreement that would have let Amazon draw power directly from the plant behind the meter, first at 300 megawatts, then expanded in 120 megawatt increments toward a ceiling of 960 megawatts. Exelon and American Electric Power intervened against the arrangement, arguing it shifted grid costs onto other ratepayers, and on November 1, 2024, FERC rejected the amended agreement on a 2 to 1 vote, with Chairman Willie Phillips dissenting on reliability grounds. Talen and Amazon did not walk away. In June 2025 the two companies restructured the deal entirely, moving from a behind the meter co location model to what Talen called a front of the meter arrangement, Susquehanna sells its output into the PJM grid as it always has, Talen becomes a retail electric supplier to Amazon under a power purchase agreement running through 2042, and PPL Electric Utilities carries the power over its transmission system rather than a private wire. The companies expect the transmission reconfiguration to take effect in spring 2026, timed to a planned refueling outage at the plant, with volume ramping toward a stated 1,920 megawatts of nuclear output by 2032.

None of those campus scale figures describe this single building. The 1125 Electron Avenue structure itself was reported by DatacenterDynamics at 48 megawatts of capacity, a number tied to the original Cumulus Data shell rather than to any Amazon operated IT load, and no source found in this research states a critical IT load, a diesel standby figure, or an onsite generation figure specific to this building under Amazon's operation. Given the scale of construction reported in trade press since the 2024 sale, it is likely additional buildings have gone up on the same parcel since, but this record concerns the single mapped structure. What remains undocumented publicly is the current occupancy status of the original Cumulus shell, any Luzerne County permit numbers tied to its later fitout by Amazon, and any tax agreement specific to this parcel, as opposed to the statewide sales tax exemption on data center equipment that Pennsylvania has offered under a 2016 law expanded in 2021.

profile.capacity_note: Not published at the individual building level. AWS and Talen Energy have disclosed campus-wide power figures: an approximately 960 megawatt data center campus purchased from Talen in 2024, and a 2025 power purchase agreement for up to 1.92 gigawatts of Susquehanna's output delivered via the grid, ramping to full volume by 2032. Neither company has broken these figures down to this specific building.
profile.facility_note: This building is registered in mapping data as Amazon AWS PHL. AWS and Talen Energy have not published which specific structure on the Susquehanna-adjacent campus this designation refers to, or its individual capacity, relative to the campus-wide megawatt figures disclosed in their agreements.
profile.research_note: Building specific MW figure (48 MW) is from DCD reporting on the original Cumulus Data powered shell, predates Amazon fitout. Campus scale figures (300 to 960 MW proposed and rejected ISA, 1,920 MW 2025 PPA) apply to the whole 1,200 acre Susquehanna parcel, not this single OSM way. Do not merge campus figures into this facility's four power columns. Address verified: OSM housenumber 1125 Electron Ave matches CoStar/DCD reporting on the Cumulus/Talen/AWS site adjacent to Susquehanna Steam Electric Station.
profile.community_note: Pennsylvania's Department of Community and Economic Development framed Amazon's wider Pennsylvania investment, which spans this Luzerne County campus and a second site in Bucks County, as worth at least 1,250 permanent high tech jobs, alongside thousands of construction positions and a 10 million dollar state commitment to local workforce training. Reporting since has cautioned that permanent onsite roles at data centers of this kind tend toward security, landscaping, and a small technical staff rather than large payrolls, and neither Salem Township nor Berwick borough has published its own count of jobs or tax revenue tied specifically to this building.
profile.regional_context: The Susquehanna nuclear plant, operated by Talen Energy near Berwick in Columbia County, Pennsylvania, sits within the PJM Interconnection, the regional grid operator covering most of Pennsylvania and a swath of the mid-Atlantic and Midwest. AWS's arrangement there is among the highest-profile examples nationally of a hyperscale cloud operator contracting directly for nuclear power to serve a data center campus, and it drew regulatory scrutiny from FERC and objections from grid operators including AEP Ohio and Exelon before the companies restructured the deal as a standard grid power purchase agreement. Pennsylvania's broader push to attract data center investment, including Amazon's $20 billion statewide commitment, has been publicly framed by Governor Josh Shapiro's administration as a strategy to pair the state's existing nuclear and gas generation capacity with new large-load industrial demand.

reading.body:
This building sits on a nuclear plant's grounds in Berwick, Pennsylvania, connected to the Susquehanna Steam Electric Station operated by Talen Energy. The structure was built by Cumulus Data as a 300,000 square foot powered shell, completed in 2023, then purchased by Amazon Web Services as part of a $650 million acquisition of the entire 1,200 acre campus in March 2024. The building itself was reported by DatacenterDynamics at 48 megawatts of capacity under its original operator, but no current IT load figure has been published since Amazon's fitout.

Amazon and Talen have disclosed a 1.92 gigawatt power purchase agreement for the entire campus, ramping to full volume by 2032, but have not broken this figure down to individual buildings. The original proposal for 960 megawatts of behind-the-meter power was rejected by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission in November 2024 on a 2 to 1 vote. The companies restructured the deal in June 2025 as a standard grid power purchase agreement, with Talen selling output into PJM and PPL Electric Utilities carrying the power to Amazon via its transmission system, now expected to take effect in spring 2026. This building's current occupancy status and any fitout permits or tax agreements specific to this parcel remain undocumented publicly.

Pennsylvania has 14 mapped data center facilities, of which only four have published megawatt figures. This campus ranks fifth by published capacity within the state. The arrangement represents one of the highest-profile examples nationally of a hyperscale operator contracting for nuclear power to serve a data center campus, and drew regulatory scrutiny before the reconfiguration as a grid purchase.
